runs.text: ASC Simphonic II, LLC (the “SPV”) is a Delaware limited liability company organized for the sole purpose of acquiring and holding shares of Series Seed Preferred Stock and associated Warrants of Simphonic, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Simphonic” or the “Portfolio Company”). The SPV is offering Class B Common Units (the “Class B Units” or the “Interests”) to a limited number of accredited investors in order to fund the SPV’s investment in Simphonic’s ongoing Series Seed Preferred Stock financing. AltSpot Capital, LLC is the Manager and Tax Representative of the SPV.

Simphonic operates a software-as-a-service platform branded as “Simphonic Care,” designed to provide complete care management for residential and long-term care facilities. According to information published by Simphonic, the platform enables multi-facility operators to centralize operations, optimize staffing, deliver structured care plans, and leverage an AI assistant for resident-level inquiries and care insights. Simphonic publicly indicates that its platform is in use across more than 500 care facilities and supports tens of thousands of residents.

Simphonic is conducting a non-brokered private placement of Series Seed Preferred Stock at a price of $0.3667 per share, reflecting a post-money valuation of approximately $13 million. The aggregate Series B raise is $500,000 to $2,000,000. The SPV intends to participate as a Series B investor with a $588,235 maximum offering amount; after payment of the 5% Management Fee, the 5% Origination and Structuring Fee, and funding of the 5% Operating Reserve, the SPV expects to invest approximately $500,000 in the Series Seed Preferred (representing approximately 1,363,512 shares) and to receive associated Warrants in accordance with the Term Sheet.

In addition to a customary 1x non-participating liquidation preference, the Series Seed Preferred carries Revenue Participation Rights pursuant to which 5% of monthly gross revenue is distributed pro rata to Series A and Series B holders (in months in which gross revenue is at least $84,000), until each such holder has received cumulative distributions of 1.5x of its purchase price. These Revenue Participation Rights terminate upon Simphonic’s completion of a Qualifying Up Round (a subsequent equity financing of at least $2 million at a post-money valuation of at least $17 million). Each Series B investor also receives Warrants to purchase Common Stock at the Issue Price equal to 30% of its principal Series B investment, less Revenue Participation Rights received or payable.

This Memorandum is intended to assist prospective investors in evaluating the Offering and should be read together with the Operating Agreement and the Term Sheet. It is not intended to provide a complete description of Simphonic or its business, prospects, or financial condition. Prospective investors are encouraged to conduct their own due diligence and to consult with their own legal, tax, and financial advisors before making an investment decision.
A. Overview

Simphonic, Inc. is a Delaware corporation that develops and markets a cloud-based care management platform under the “Simphonic Care” brand. The platform is purpose-built for operators of care facilities — including senior living, assisted living, skilled nursing, memory care, and similar settings — and is intended to streamline multi-facility operations, optimize staff assignments, and enhance resident care through AI-powered insights and intelligent care planning. Simphonic’s public website is located at https://simphonic.ai/.
B. Product and Platform
Based on information published by Simphonic, the Simphonic Care platform offers an integrated suite of capabilities, including:
Multi-Facility Management. A centralized dashboard allowing operators to manage multiple care facilities with consolidated oversight and configurable, facility-specific rules.
Role-Based Staff Assignment. Intelligent matching of caregivers to residents based on roles, qualifications, certifications, and availability.
Smart Shift Management. Shift scheduling and assignment optimization designed to ensure adequate coverage and continuity of care.
Comprehensive Care Plans. Customizable care plan templates and protocols for assessing resident needs, setting care goals, and tracking delivery.

AI Care Assistant. A natural-language interface that allows caregivers and administrators to query resident-level data (for example, daily intake, medication adherence, vision or mobility status) and receive contextual insights and recommendations.
Advanced Analytics. Reporting on care metrics, staff performance, and resident outcomes to support operational and clinical decision-making.

Simphonic publicly states that its platform is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, that it is trusted by more than 500 care facilities, that it supports more than 10,000 active users and residents, and that customers report meaningful efficiency gains following implementation. These statements are made by Simphonic and have not been independently verified by the SPV or the Manager.
C. Market Opportunity

Simphonic operates at the intersection of three large and growing markets: senior and post-acute care services; healthcare information technology; and applied artificial intelligence. The U.S. care facility market continues to expand as the population ages, while operators face sustained pressure on margins driven by labor shortages, regulatory complexity, rising acuity, and demands for measurable quality outcomes. Software platforms that can demonstrably reduce administrative burden, improve staff utilization, and document quality of care are well-positioned to capture share within this environment, although competition is significant and operator purchasing cycles can be long.
D. Customers and Traction

Simphonic publicly reports adoption across more than 500 care facilities, with implementation timelines that typically include initial setup and training, data migration, go-live, and ongoing optimization. Specific revenue, customer concentration, retention, and unit economics figures have not been independently verified by the SPV. The Term Sheet contemplates Revenue Participation Rights triggered when monthly gross revenue equals or exceeds $84,000, indicating that Simphonic expects to operate near or above this threshold during the period the Revenue Participation Rights are in effect; however, no representation is made as to current or future revenue levels.
E. Intellectual Property and Compliance

Simphonic’s product depends on proprietary software, machine learning models, and integrations with third-party services. Simphonic states that its platform is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, both of which are material to its ability to serve healthcare customers. Continued compliance with health data, privacy, and security laws (including HIPAA, HITECH, applicable state laws such as the California Consumer Privacy Act, and emerging AI-specific regulations) is essential to Simphonic’s business.

runs.text: Simphonic is conducting a non-brokered private placement of Series Seed Preferred Stock pursuant to a non-binding term sheet executed by Simphonic (the “Term Sheet”). The principal terms of the Series Seed Preferred and the SPV’s anticipated investment in Simphonic are summarized below. The terms below remain subject in all respects to the negotiation and execution of definitive transaction documents (including a stock purchase agreement, an amended and restated certificate of incorporation, an investors’ rights agreement, a right of first refusal and co-sale agreement, a voting agreement, and a warrant agreement (collectively, the “Definitive Documents”)). The Definitive Documents may differ in material respects from the Term Sheet.
A. Issue Price; Valuation; Round Size

The Series Seed Preferred is being sold at a price of $0.3667 per share, reflecting a post-money valuation of approximately $13 million. The aggregate Series Seed Preferred round size is between $500,000 and $2,000,000. The Term Sheet imposes a $100,000 minimum subscription at the Simphonic level, which the SPV expects to satisfy in the aggregate.
B. SPV’s Anticipated Investment

Based on a Maximum Offering Amount of $588,235, after payment of the Management Fee (approximately $29,412), the Origination and Structuring Fee (approximately $29,412), and funding of the Operating Reserve (approximately $29,412), the SPV expects to invest approximately $500,000 in the Series Seed Preferred at $0.3667 per share, representing approximately 1,363,512 shares of Series Seed Preferred. The SPV expects to receive associated Warrants in accordance with the Term Sheet (calculated as 30% of the SPV’s principal Series B investment, less RPR distributions received or payable, with an exercise price of $0.3667 per share). Actual share counts will be subject to rounding and to confirmation of the SPV’s allocation by Simphonic.
C. Liquidation Preference

The Series Seed Preferred is entitled to a 1x non-participating liquidation preference over Common Stock and pari passu with the Series A Preferred. Following the payment of the 1x preferential return on the Series A and Series Seed Preferred, remaining liquidation proceeds are distributed pro rata among holders of Common Stock, Series A Preferred, and Series Seed Preferred. Revenue Participation Rights are not payable in connection with a sale or liquidation event.
D. Revenue Participation Rights

As an additional return mechanism, the Series A and Series Seed Preferred share a Revenue Participation Right (the “RPR”). For each month in which Simphonic’s collected gross revenue equals or exceeds $84,000, 5% of such monthly gross revenue is allocated to a pool that is distributed pro rata to Series A and Series Seed Preferred holders quarterly in arrears. Distributions continue until each such holder has received cumulative RPR distributions equal to 1.5x of the amount paid for its Series A and/or Series Seed Preferred shares.

Importantly, the RPR terminates automatically and prospectively upon Simphonic’s completion of a Qualifying Up Round (defined as a subsequent equity financing of at least $2 million at a post-money valuation of at least $17 million). No make-whole or compensatory payment is owed to Series A or Series B holders on account of the termination of the RPR. As a result, the RPR may produce limited or no aggregate distributions if Simphonic completes a Qualifying Up Round shortly after the Series B closing. RPR distributions received by the SPV will be subject to the SPV’s distribution waterfall (including the Carried Interest after Class B Members have recovered their Unreturned Capital).
E. Warrants

Each Series B investor (including the SPV) will receive warrants to purchase Common Stock at the Issue Price ($0.3667 per share). The number of Warrants is equal to thirty percent (30%) of such investor’s principal Series B investment, less any RPR distributions received or payable for any period prior to exercise. The Warrants expire immediately prior to the closing of Simphonic’s next equity financing that is at a pre-money valuation of at least $11 million. As a result, the Warrants may have a short life if Simphonic raises additional equity in the near term, and Warrant holders will need to make a timely decision to exercise to capture any in-the-money value. The Manager will determine, in its sole discretion, whether to exercise, sell, or allow the Warrants to lapse. To the extent the Manager elects to exercise, the cash required to do so is expected to be funded from the Operating Reserve or, if necessary, by capital call under Section 2.5 of the Operating Agreement.
F. Governance; Information Rights

Following the closing, Simphonic’s Board of Directors is expected to consist of Steven Blake (founder), Matthew Paroly and Eric Woo. The Term Sheet provides that any holder of more than 2% of Simphonic’s outstanding shares may designate a non-voting observer to attend Board meetings. Based on the SPV’s anticipated holdings (approximately 3.85% on a fully-diluted basis, without giving effect to Warrants), the SPV intends to designate a non-voting Board observer (subject to customary confidentiality and other restrictions). The SPV will not have a voting Board seat or operational control over Simphonic. Shareholders will have ongoing access to financial and other performance information from Simphonic, on terms to be set forth in the Definitive Documents.
G. Pre-Emptive Rights, Tag-Along, Drag-Along, ROFR

The Term Sheet contemplates customary stockholder protections at the Simphonic level, including: (i) pro rata pre-emptive rights to participate in subsequent Simphonic equity issuances; (ii) tag-along rights triggered when a sale would result in a third party acquiring 50% or more of Simphonic’s shares; (iii) drag-along rights pursuant to which shareholders owning 60% or more of Simphonic may compel remaining shareholders to participate in a sale of all or substantially all of Simphonic on the same terms; and (iv) a right of first refusal on transfers, with shares first offered pro rata and then on an equal basis to other Simphonic shareholders. Revenue Participation Rights are not payable in connection with any such sale. The Manager will exercise (or refrain from exercising) all such rights on behalf of the SPV in its sole discretion.
H. Closing

The Series Seed Preferred financing is targeted to close no later than June 1, 2026, subject to extension by Simphonic in its sole discretion. The Manager intends to time the SPV’s closing to permit funding of its allocation by Simphonic’s closing deadline.
I. Use of Proceeds (Simphonic Level)

Per the Term Sheet, Simphonic intends to use the proceeds of the Series Seed Preferred financing primarily for general corporate and working capital purposes, including, without limitation, enterprise customer onboarding, product deployment, and continued platform development.

The Manager believes that an investment in Simphonic Series Seed Preferred (and associated Warrants) through the SPV offers a compelling, though risky, opportunity for the following principal reasons:

Large and Defensible End Market. The senior and post-acute care market is large, fragmented, and underpenetrated by modern software. Care facilities increasingly require purpose-built platforms to manage clinical and operational complexity, and the cost of switching established systems creates meaningful customer stickiness.

Vertical AI Application. Simphonic’s AI Care Assistant applies modern natural-language and machine learning techniques to a high-value, data-rich vertical. Vertical-specific AI products that are anchored in proprietary workflow data have the potential to compound advantages over time relative to horizontal AI tools.

Demonstrated Adoption. Simphonic publicly reports more than 500 deployed facilities and significant active user counts. While these statements are unverified by the SPV, they suggest the company has moved beyond pilot stage and is generating recurring revenue from real operators.

Regulatory Tailwinds. Increasing regulatory focus on quality of care, staffing minimums, and documentation creates structural demand for software that can produce defensible records, support audits, and reduce reliance on overburdened caregivers.

Structural Downside Protection. The 1x non-participating liquidation preference (pari passu with Series A) provides a measure of downside protection in a sale scenario, ranking the SPV ahead of Common Stock for the return of its invested capital.

Cash-Flow Component via Revenue Participation Rights. The RPR is structured to deliver early-period cash returns of up to 1.5x of subscription price (subject to monthly revenue exceeding $84,000 and to early termination upon a Qualifying Up Round), partially de-risking the investment if Simphonic’s revenue trajectory continues.

Warrant Upside. The Warrants provide additional equity exposure at the Issue Price, with potential to capture upside in advance of Simphonic’s next priced round (subject to expiration of the Warrants in connection with such next round).

Sponsor Familiarity. The Manager is affiliated with ASC Simphonic LLC, a Series A holder in Simphonic, and accordingly the Manager has prior diligence and relationship history with the Portfolio Company. See “Conflicts of Interest.”

These factors are not exhaustive and should be considered in conjunction with the risks described in “Risk Factors” below. The investment thesis set forth herein is the Manager’s view based on currently available information and is subject to change. There can be no assurance that any of the foregoing expectations will be realized or that an investment in the Interests will be profitable.
A. Formation and Purpose

ASC Simphonic II, LLC was formed under the Delaware Limited Liability Company Act (the “Act”) pursuant to a Certificate of Formation filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware. The SPV is a single-purpose investment vehicle. Pursuant to Section 1.4 of the Operating Agreement, the SPV’s sole purpose is to hold securities of Simphonic and to engage in any other lawful act or activity reasonably related to that purpose.
B. Capital Structure
The SPV’s capital is divided into two classes of Common Units, as set forth in Section 2.1.2 of the Operating Agreement:

Class A Common Units. One (1) Class A Unit will be issued to the Manager (or its designee). The Class A Unit carries one vote per Unit and the right to receive the Carried Interest, but otherwise has no economic rights and is entitled to no return of capital except in respect of the Carried Interest. The Class A Unit is intended to constitute a “profits interest” within the meaning of IRS Revenue Procedure 93-27 and Revenue Procedure 2001-43.

Class B Common Units. Up to 588,235 Class B Units will be issued to investors at $1.00 per Unit. The Class B Units have no voting rights or rights to participate in management of the SPV (except as expressly provided in the Operating Agreement and the Act) and are entitled to the economic distributions described in this Memorandum.
C. Structure of the Investment

The SPV will subscribe for Series Seed Preferred (and related Warrants) directly from Simphonic at the Issue Price set forth in the Term Sheet. The Manager will negotiate and execute the Definitive Documents on behalf of the SPV. The SPV does not expect to obtain a voting seat on Simphonic’s Board of Directors. To the extent the SPV holds more than 2% of Simphonic’s outstanding shares (which is currently anticipated), the SPV intends to designate a non-voting Board observer. The SPV’s rights as a shareholder of Simphonic will be limited to those set forth in the Definitive Documents and applicable law.
D. Operating Agreement

The rights and obligations of the SPV’s Members are governed by the Operating Agreement, which each investor will be required to execute (or be deemed to have executed pursuant to the Subscription Agreement). Among other matters, the Operating Agreement governs (i) capital contributions and capital calls (Article 2), (ii) admission of additional Members (Article 3), (iii) management by the Manager (Article 4), (iv) allocations of profits and losses and distributions (Article 5), (v) transfer and assignment of Interests (Article 6), (vi) accounting, records, and tax matters (Article 7), (vii) dissolution and winding up (Article 8), (viii) indemnification (Article 9), (ix) Member representations, warranties, and covenants (Article 10), and (x) miscellaneous matters including arbitration and governing law (Article 11). Investors should read the Operating Agreement carefully before subscribing. Capitalized terms used in this Memorandum and not otherwise defined have the meanings set forth in the Operating Agreement.
E. Voting and Consent of SPV Investors

Pursuant to Sections 2.1.2 and 4.3 of the Operating Agreement, holders of Class B Units have no right to participate in management of the SPV. The Manager has “full, complete, and exclusive authority, power, and discretion to manage and control the business, property, and affairs” of the SPV (Section 4.1), including the authority to vote, exercise, or refrain from exercising rights with respect to the Portfolio Securities. Class B Members will not have the right to direct the Manager’s actions on a security-by-security or matter-by-matter basis.
F. Removal of Manager

Under Section 4.1 of the Operating Agreement, the Manager may be removed only by the Member Majority Interest (a majority of issued and outstanding Common Units) and only for “Cause,” which is narrowly defined to mean (a) the Manager’s knowing participation in fraud, embezzlement, theft, or similar acts that materially and adversely affect Company property or business; (b) the Manager’s intentional infliction of damage to Company property causing a material loss; or (c) the Manager’s conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony. Investors should not invest if they require broader or more flexible removal rights.

A. The Manager

B. Tax Representative

The Tax Representative has broad authority to represent the SPV in tax matters, make tax elections (including elections under Sections 6221(b) and 6226 of the Code), and bind the Members in connection with such matters. The SPV intends to elect the application of Section 6226 of the Code (push-out election); see “Risk Factors” and “Certain U.S. Federal Income Tax Considerations.”
C. Key Persons

The principal individual(s) responsible for managing the SPV on behalf of AltSpot Capital, LLC will be Ryan Billings and Tyler Lucas (each, a “Key Person”). Brief biographical information regarding each Key Person, including relevant investment, operational, and industry experience, will be provided in an annex to this Memorandum or under separate cover. Investors should not invest in the Interests if they are not satisfied with the qualifications and background of the Key Persons.
D. Manager Liability and Fiduciary Standard

Section 4.6 of the Operating Agreement provides that the Manager is not liable to the SPV or to any Member for any loss or damage sustained by the SPV or any Member, unless the loss or damage resulted from the Manager’s intentional misconduct or fraud. The Members agree that the fiduciary duties of the Manager are limited to the maximum extent permitted by the Act. As permitted by Delaware law, this materially reduces the Manager’s exposure to liability and the duties owed by the Manager to the Members in comparison to the default rules under Delaware law.
E. Indemnification

Article 9 of the Operating Agreement provides for broad indemnification of, and advancement of expenses to, the Manager, the officers of the SPV, and any person who is or was a Manager, officer, or Member of the SPV in connection with any threatened, pending, or completed action, suit, or proceeding by reason of such status. This indemnification right does not apply where the indemnitee has committed fraud or willful misconduct.

articles.title: COMPENSATION OF THE MANAGER; FEES AND EXPENSES

runs.text: A. Management Fee (Section 2.7)

The Manager will receive a one-time Management Fee equal to 5% of aggregate capital contributions made at each closing. This Management Fee represents the prepayment, in full, of all annual management fees that would otherwise be payable to the Manager during the term of the SPV, and no further management fees of any kind will be payable to the Manager. Based on a $588,235 raise, the Management Fee equals approximately $29,412. The Management Fee is paid out of the SPV’s assets and is disregarded for purposes of calculating any Member’s capital contribution, Capital Account, Unreturned Capital, Percentage Interest, or number of Class B Units. As a result, Members effectively bear the Management Fee through a reduction in invested capital, but their percentage interests, distribution rights, and Unreturned Capital are calculated as though the full $588,235 were available for investment.
B. Origination and Structuring Fee (Section 2.9)

The Manager will also receive a one-time Origination and Structuring Fee equal to 5% of aggregate capital contributions made at each closing, in consideration of documenting, forming, and organizing the SPV, including legal, third-party consulting and diligence expenses, entity-formation costs, and the Manager’s personnel and resources expended in connection therewith. Based on a $588,235 raise, the Origination and Structuring Fee equals approximately $29,412. Like the Management Fee, the Origination and Structuring Fee is paid out of the SPV’s assets and is disregarded for purposes of calculating any Member’s capital contribution, Capital Account, Unreturned Capital, Percentage Interest, or number of Class B Units.
C. Carried Interest (Sections 5.1.16, 5.7)

The Carried Interest is equal to 20% of cumulative Distributable Cash and other distributions, payable to the holder(s) of Class A Units, after each Class B Member has received cumulative distributions equal to such Member’s Unreturned Capital. The Class A Units are intended to constitute a profits interest within the meaning of Rev. Proc. 93-27 and Rev. Proc. 2001-43. The Carried Interest applies to all categories of distributions — including RPR distributions passed through from Simphonic, Warrant exercise proceeds, and proceeds from the disposition of Series Seed Preferred — once Class B Members have recovered their Unreturned Capital. The Carried Interest does not apply to (i) Tax Distributions under Section 5.6 (which are credited against later distributions) or (ii) returns of unused Operating Reserve under Section 2.8 (which are returned solely to Class B Members).
D. Operating Reserve (Section 2.8)

At closing, 5% of aggregate capital contributions (approximately $29,412 based on a $588,235 raise) is set aside as an Operating Reserve to fund Company Expenses. The Operating Reserve is the primary source of funds for Company Expenses. Any portion of the Operating Reserve not required to pay anticipated Company Expenses (including any portion remaining at dissolution) is returned to Class B Members pro rata, free of Carried Interest, and reduces each such Member’s Unreturned Capital.
E. Capital Calls (Section 2.5)

If Operating Reserve is exhausted and additional Company Expenses arise, the Manager may send written notice to all Members to contribute additional cash on a pro rata basis at a per-unit price equal to the price per unit paid for the initial Class B Units ($1.00 per Unit). Members must contribute their pro rata share within ten (10) days of notice. A Member that fails to participate in a capital call will be diluted in favor of the contributing Members. Members are not personally liable for SPV obligations, but a failure to participate in a capital call has dilutive consequences.
F. Other Company Expenses

Pursuant to Section 2.5, the SPV bears all operating expenses attributable to its or the Manager’s activities, including: organizational and liquidation expenses; sales, transfer, or governmental taxes and fees; brokerage and similar charges; litigation expenses (including indemnification); banking, accounting, appraisal, legal, custodial, and registration services; and tax preparation and Schedule K-1 expenses. Pursuant to the Term Sheet, all parties to the Series Seed Preferred financing are responsible for their own legal, advisory, and other expenses related to the Simphonic-level transaction; accordingly, the SPV (and not Simphonic) bears its own such expenses.
A. Distribution Waterfall (Section 5.7)
Distributable Cash is distributed by the SPV in accordance with the following waterfall under Section 5.7 of the Operating Agreement:
Return of Unreturned Capital. First, to each Class B Member in proportion to such Member’s Unreturned Capital, until each Class B Member’s Unreturned Capital has been reduced to zero.
80/20 Split. Thereafter, 80% to Class B Members pro rata in accordance with each Member’s Percentage Interest, and 20% to the holder(s) of Class A Units in respect of the Carried Interest.

“Unreturned Capital” means each Class B Member’s capital contributions, reduced by the cumulative distributions to such Member under Section 2.8 (return of unused Operating Reserve), Section 5.6 (Tax Distributions), Section 5.7.1.1, and Section 5.7.2.1. As a result, Tax Distributions and returns of unused Operating Reserve reduce Unreturned Capital and accelerate the point at which the Carried Interest begins to accrue.
B. Liquidating Distributions (Section 5.7.2)

Upon a Liquidation Event, the SPV’s assets are distributed in the same priority as Section 5.7.1: first, to Class B Members in proportion to Unreturned Capital; and then, 80% to Class B Members pro rata and 20% to Class A Units as Carried Interest. A “Liquidation Event” includes a sale of substantially all of the SPV’s assets, certain mergers or consolidations, or a sale of a majority of Units by Members. The distribution by Simphonic to the SPV of substantially all cash or assets attributable to the SPV’s ownership in Simphonic is also a Liquidation Event.
C. Tax Distributions (Section 5.6)

If Distributable Cash is available, the Manager is required to distribute cash to each Member in an amount sufficient to enable that Member to satisfy its estimated federal and state income tax liability with respect to allocations from the SPV, calculated assuming the highest applicable marginal rates and based on the Member’s state of residence. Tax Distributions are mandatory if Distributable Cash is available. Any Tax Distribution made to a Member is credited against subsequent distributions to that Member under Section 5.7.
D. Allocations of Net Profits and Net Losses (Section 5.2)

Net Profits and Net Losses (and individual items thereof) are allocated among the Members so as to ensure, to the greatest extent possible, that each Member’s Capital Account at the end of each fiscal year equals the amount such Member would receive if the SPV’s assets were sold at Book Value, all liabilities satisfied, and the proceeds distributed in accordance with Section 5.7. The Operating Agreement contains customary regulatory allocations relating to minimum gain chargebacks, qualified income offsets, and Section 704(c) allocations (Sections 5.3, 5.4, and 5.5).

AN INVESTMENT IN THE INTERESTS INVOLVES A HIGH DEGREE OF RISK AND IS SUITABLE ONLY FOR PERSONS OF ADEQUATE FINANCIAL MEANS WHO CAN AFFORD A LOSS OF THEIR ENTIRE INVESTMENT. PROSPECTIVE INVESTORS SHOULD CAREFULLY CONSIDER THE FOLLOWING RISKS, IN ADDITION TO THE OTHER INFORMATION SET FORTH IN THIS MEMORANDUM, BEFORE MAKING AN INVESTMENT DECISION. THE RISKS DESCRIBED BELOW ARE NOT INTENDED TO BE EXHAUSTIVE.
A. Risks Relating to the SPV and the Interests
Single-Asset Concentration.

The SPV is a single-purpose vehicle whose sole investment will be in Simphonic. The performance of the SPV will depend entirely on the performance of Simphonic. Investors will have no diversification within the SPV and could lose all or substantially all of their investment if Simphonic fails or its securities decline materially in value.
No Voting or Management Rights for Class B Members.

Class B Units have no voting rights and no right to participate in management of the SPV. The Manager has full and exclusive authority to make all decisions on behalf of the SPV, including with respect to voting Simphonic shares, exercising or allowing the Warrants to lapse, responding to drag-along notices and subsequent financings, making capital calls, and disposing of the Portfolio Securities. Class B Members will not have any meaningful ability to influence these decisions.
Manager Removal Only for Narrow Cause.

The Manager may be removed only for “Cause” as defined in Section 4.1 of the Operating Agreement — essentially fraud, intentional damage to Company property, or a felony conviction. Members may not remove the Manager for poor performance, conflicts of interest, or other reasons. Investors should be comfortable with the Manager’s continuing role for the entire term of the SPV.
Limited Fiduciary Duties; Limited Liability of Manager.

Pursuant to Section 4.6, the Manager is liable to the SPV and the Members only for losses arising from intentional misconduct or fraud, and the fiduciary duties of the Manager are limited to the maximum extent permitted by Delaware law. This standard is significantly more permissive than the default duties under Delaware law and will limit Members’ ability to bring claims against the Manager.
Broad Indemnification.

Article 9 of the Operating Agreement requires the SPV to indemnify the Manager, officers, and Members (and to advance expenses) in connection with any threatened, pending, or completed proceeding, except in the case of fraud or willful misconduct. Such indemnification reduces SPV assets available to make distributions to Members and could materially affect Members’ returns.
Capital Calls and Dilution.

Although Members are not generally required to make additional capital contributions, the Manager may issue a capital call under Section 2.5 if the Operating Reserve is insufficient to pay Company Expenses. A Member that fails to participate in a capital call will be diluted relative to contributing Members. Members should be prepared to fund a capital call or accept dilution.
Illiquidity and Transfer Restrictions.

There is no public market for the Interests, and none is expected to develop. The Interests are subject to substantial restrictions on transfer under the Securities Act, applicable state securities laws, the Operating Agreement (Article 6 — Manager consent required, with limited exceptions for Family Members), and indirectly the right-of-first-refusal regime applicable to the underlying Simphonic shares. Investors must be prepared to hold the Interests for an indefinite period and to bear the economic risk of the investment until the SPV winds up.
Dependence on the Manager.

The success of the SPV depends substantially on the abilities and judgment of the Manager and its Key Persons, including with respect to the timing of Warrant exercise, voting decisions, and responses to drag-along notices and subsequent financings. The loss of one or more Key Persons could materially adversely affect the SPV.
Limited Information Rights.

The SPV’s information rights with respect to Simphonic will be limited to those provided in the Definitive Documents. Section 7.2 of the Operating Agreement requires the SPV to provide each Member, within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year, with information sufficient to complete federal and state income tax returns and a copy of the SPV’s tax return. The Operating Agreement does not require the SPV to provide audited financial statements, periodic NAV reporting, or formal portfolio updates beyond Section 7.2 (although the Manager may elect to do so).
Mandatory Arbitration in Los Angeles.

Pursuant to Section 11.4, any controversy arising out of the Operating Agreement is subject to binding, non-appealable arbitration before the American Arbitration Association in Los Angeles, California. Members waive the right to litigate disputes in court, the right to a jury trial, and the right to appeal. The costs of arbitration are generally borne equally by the parties (although attorneys’ fees may be awarded to the prevailing party). For Members not located in California, this venue may impose meaningful additional cost and inconvenience.
Conflicts of Interest.

The Manager and its affiliates may have material conflicts of interest, including with respect to the allocation of investment opportunities, management of multiple investment vehicles, the receipt of fees, an existing affiliated holding in Simphonic’s Series A Preferred (held by ASC Simphonic LLC), and the negotiation of terms with Simphonic. See “Conflicts of Interest.”
Fees and Expenses Reduce Returns.

Investors will bear the 5% Management Fee, the 5% Origination and Structuring Fee, the 20% Carried Interest, and ongoing Company Expenses, all of which will reduce the net returns realized by investors and could exceed the SPV’s gains. The Management Fee and the Origination and Structuring Fee are each paid in full at closing regardless of how long the SPV continues and regardless of the SPV’s ultimate investment performance.
No Right of Withdrawal.

Pursuant to Section 3.2, no Member may withdraw, retire, or resign from the SPV except as set forth in Article 6 (transfer of Interests). Distributions, if any, will be made only as the Manager determines and only as RPR amounts, Warrant proceeds, or sale proceeds become available.
Tax Risks.

The U.S. federal, state, local, and non-U.S. tax consequences of an investment in the SPV are complex and uncertain. The SPV may generate taxable income to investors that exceeds the cash distributed to them in any given year. Although the Operating Agreement requires Tax Distributions when Distributable Cash is available, there can be no assurance that the SPV will have sufficient cash to make Tax Distributions in any particular year. The SPV will elect the application of Section 6226 of the Code (push-out election) under Section 7.4, which means that any tax adjustments resulting from an IRS audit will be allocated to the Members for the reviewed year, and Members are required to take such adjustments into account on their personal returns. Members are required by Section 7.4.3 to indemnify the SPV against tax liabilities resulting from a Member’s failure to comply. See “Certain U.S. Federal Income Tax Considerations.”
B. Risks Relating to the Series Seed Preferred and Warrants
Non-Binding Term Sheet.

The terms of the Series Seed Preferred and Warrants described in this Memorandum are derived from a non-binding Term Sheet. The Definitive Documents have not yet been executed and may differ in material respects from the Term Sheet, including with respect to the rights, preferences, and privileges of the Series Seed Preferred, the mechanics of the RPR, the terms of the Warrants, and governance and shareholder protections.
Limited Liquidation Preference.

The Series Seed Preferred has a 1x non-participating liquidation preference, pari passu with the Series A Preferred. In a downside sale scenario, the SPV will share its preferential return with Series A holders on a pari passu basis. After payment of the 1x preference on Series A and Series B, remaining proceeds are distributed pro rata across Common, Series A, and Series B; this structure may yield modest returns in mid-case sale outcomes.
Revenue Participation Rights Are Contingent and Capped.

The RPR depends on Simphonic’s ability to generate at least $84,000 in collected gross revenue in any given month. There can be no assurance that Simphonic will reach or sustain this threshold. The RPR is also subject to a 1.5x cumulative cap and to early termination upon a Qualifying Up Round (defined as a subsequent equity financing of at least $2 million at a post-money valuation of at least $17 million). If Simphonic completes a Qualifying Up Round shortly after the closing of the SPV’s investment, the RPR may produce minimal aggregate distributions, and no make-whole or other compensation will be owed. RPR distributions received by the SPV will be subject to the SPV’s distribution waterfall (including the Carried Interest after Class B Members have recovered Unreturned Capital).
Warrant Risks.

The Warrants are exercisable at $0.3667 per share for Common Stock (which ranks behind the Series A and Series B liquidation preferences). The Warrant share count is calculated as 30% of the principal Series B investment, less RPR distributions received or payable for the period prior to exercise; as a result, the Warrants effectively decline as RPR distributions are paid, and the timing of exercise materially affects coverage. The Warrants expire immediately prior to the closing of Simphonic’s next equity financing at a pre-money valuation of at least $11 million, which may result in only a short window for exercise (and may include a window during which the Warrants are out of the money or in which exercise requires advancing cash that the SPV may not have on hand). To exercise the Warrants, the SPV may need to draw on the Operating Reserve or call additional capital from Members under Section 2.5; if Members fail to participate in such a capital call, they will be diluted, and if the SPV has insufficient cash to fund exercise, the Warrants may lapse worthless.
Down-Round and Anti-Dilution Risk.

The Term Sheet does not specify the anti-dilution rights of the Series Seed Preferred. Depending on what is ultimately included in the Definitive Documents, the SPV may have limited or no protection against dilutive future financings (including any future down round). Even with broad-based weighted average anti-dilution protection, future financings could materially dilute the SPV’s percentage ownership of Simphonic.
Founder and Voting Concentration.

Based on the pro forma capitalization, Steven Blake (the founder) holds approximately 46.75% of Simphonic’s fully-diluted equity, and the Board is expected to consist solely of Steven Blake, Matthew Paroly and Eric Woo. The SPV will not have a voting Board seat. Founder and small-Board control could affect strategic, operational, financing, and exit decisions in ways that may not align with the SPV’s interests.
Drag-Along Risk.

Shareholders owning 60% or more of Simphonic may compel the SPV to participate in a sale of all or substantially all of Simphonic on the same terms as the dragging shareholders. If such a transaction occurs at a low valuation, the SPV may be required to sell its Series Seed Preferred at a price that produces little or no return after payment of fees, expenses, and pari passu Series A liquidation preference. RPR is not payable in connection with such a sale.
Right of First Refusal on Transfers.

Any transfer of Simphonic shares is subject to a right of first refusal in favor of other Simphonic shareholders, first on a pro rata basis and then on an equal basis. This may delay or prevent the SPV from selling Portfolio Securities in a secondary transaction at favorable prices.
Limited Governance Rights.

The Term Sheet contemplates only non-voting observer rights for shareholders holding more than 2% (which the SPV expects to exceed based on its anticipated allocation). The SPV will not have the ability to direct Simphonic’s strategy, capital structure, or executive decisions.
C. Risks Relating to Simphonic and Its Business
Early-Stage Company Risk.

Simphonic is a privately held company that is or may be in an early or growth stage of development. Such companies are subject to greater risks than more established businesses, including limited operating history, dependence on a small management team, limited financial resources, the need for additional financing, and substantial uncertainty as to future revenue, profitability, and cash flow. Many privately held early-stage and growth-stage companies fail.
Need for Additional Capital and Dilution.

The Series Seed Preferred round size of $500,000 to $2,000,000 may be insufficient to fund Simphonic’s long-term operating plan. Simphonic may require additional capital in the future, and such financings, if available at all, may be on terms that are dilutive to the SPV’s investment, may include preferences senior to the Series Seed Preferred, and may involve covenants that restrict Simphonic’s business. There can be no assurance that Simphonic will be able to obtain financing on acceptable terms or at all.
Competition.

Simphonic operates in a competitive market that includes established electronic health record (EHR) and care management vendors, point solutions for staffing and scheduling, and emerging AI-native entrants. Many competitors have substantially greater financial, technical, and marketing resources than Simphonic. Increased competition could pressure pricing, lengthen sales cycles, and reduce Simphonic’s ability to win and retain customers.
Customer Concentration and Retention.

Simphonic’s revenue may be concentrated among a limited number of customers, and the loss of one or more significant customers could materially adversely affect Simphonic, including by reducing or eliminating monthly revenue below the $84,000 threshold required to trigger RPR distributions.
Healthcare Regulatory Risk.

Simphonic’s business is subject to extensive and evolving regulation, including HIPAA and HITECH, state privacy and security laws (including the California Consumer Privacy Act and similar regimes), state licensing requirements applicable to long-term care providers, and Medicare and Medicaid program requirements applicable to its customers. Compliance with such laws is costly, and any actual or alleged violation could result in significant fines, injunctions, contractual liability, reputational harm, and loss of customers.
Data Privacy and Security.

Simphonic processes sensitive resident health information and other personally identifiable information. A cybersecurity incident, data breach, ransomware attack, insider threat, or vendor compromise could result in regulatory investigations, breach notification obligations, civil liability, contractual penalties, customer churn, and reputational damage, any of which could materially adversely affect Simphonic and the value of the Portfolio Securities.
AI-Specific Risks.

Simphonic’s product incorporates artificial intelligence and machine learning components, including a natural-language AI Care Assistant. AI systems are subject to risks including, without limitation, model errors, hallucinations, bias, training data limitations, dependence on third-party foundation models, and rapidly evolving regulation. Inaccurate AI outputs in a clinical or care setting could give rise to professional liability or product liability claims.
Product Liability and Care-Related Liability.

Although Simphonic provides software (and not direct clinical care), errors or omissions in the platform could be alleged to have contributed to resident harm or substandard care, exposing Simphonic to litigation, indemnification claims by customers, and reputational harm. Insurance may be insufficient to cover all such claims.
Dependence on Third-Party Infrastructure.

Simphonic depends on third-party cloud hosting, communications, identity, AI/ML, and integration providers. Outages, price increases, or termination of relationships with such providers could materially affect Simphonic’s operations.
Intellectual Property.

Simphonic’s competitive position depends on its ability to protect its proprietary technology and to avoid infringing third-party rights. Simphonic could become subject to claims that it infringes third-party intellectual property rights, which could result in costly litigation, injunctions, royalties, and product redesigns.
Reliance on Key Personnel.

Simphonic’s success depends on the continued services of its founders (in particular Steven Blake), executive officers, and key engineering, product, sales, and clinical personnel. The loss of any such person could materially affect Simphonic.
Macroeconomic and Industry Conditions.

Simphonic’s business is exposed to macroeconomic conditions affecting its customers, including reimbursement pressures, labor markets, interest rates, inflation, and broader healthcare policy developments.
Valuation and Limited Exit Opportunities.

The $13 million post-money valuation reflects negotiations between Simphonic and Series B investors and embeds assumptions about Simphonic’s future performance that may prove incorrect. The Portfolio Securities will be illiquid, and there can be no assurance that an exit event will occur within any particular time frame, on favorable terms, or at all. The SPV’s ability to realize value depends on such an event, on RPR distributions, and on the in-the-money exercise of the Warrants.
Forward-Looking Statements.

This Memorandum contains forward-looking statements concerning Simphonic and the SPV. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied. Investors should not place undue reliance on any forward-looking statement.
The Manager and its affiliates may have a number of actual or potential conflicts of interest with the SPV and its investors, including the following:

Pre-Existing Affiliated Investment in Simphonic. ASC Simphonic LLC, an affiliate of the Manager, currently holds 600,000 shares of Series A Preferred Stock of Simphonic (representing approximately 1.69% of Simphonic’s fully-diluted equity), and accordingly may receive RPR distributions on a pari passu basis with the SPV. The interests of ASC Simphonic LLC may not be aligned in all respects with those of the SPV (for example, with respect to the timing and structure of a Qualifying Up Round, exit transactions, or the exercise of pre-emptive rights).

Other Investment Vehicles. The Manager and its affiliates may organize, manage, or advise other investment vehicles or accounts (such as ASC Simphonic LLC and any successor or parallel vehicles) that may invest in Simphonic, in competitors of Simphonic, or in other companies. Allocations of investment opportunities and follow-on rights among such vehicles may give rise to conflicts.

Fees and Carried Interest. The Manager will receive fees and Carried Interest from the SPV. The structure of these economics may incentivize the Manager to make investment, holding, or disposition decisions — including with respect to the timing of Warrant exercise and response to drag-along notices — that prioritize the Manager’s economic interests over those of investors. The one-time, prepaid Management Fee structure also creates an incentive for the Manager to wind up the SPV (and avoid extending its term beyond what is necessary).

Pre-Existing Relationships. The Manager, its principals, or their affiliates may have pre-existing relationships with Simphonic or its securityholders, officers, directors, advisors, or employees, including as investors, advisors, board members, or service providers.

Side Letters. The Manager may waive the $50,000 Minimum Subscription Amount or otherwise enter into side letters or similar arrangements with one or more investors granting them rights, terms, or economics not available to other investors, all to the extent permitted by the Operating Agreement.
Service Providers. The Manager may engage service providers (including legal counsel, administrators, and tax preparers) that have other relationships with the Manager or its affiliates.

Valuation. The Manager will be responsible for valuing the Portfolio Securities (including for purposes of determining Book Value and the timing of Liquidation Events), which may affect reporting to investors and the calculation of certain fees and the Carried Interest.

Tax Representative. AltSpot Capital, LLC will serve as Tax Representative under Section 7.4 with broad authority to make tax elections and bind Members. The Tax Representative’s decisions may have different tax effects on different Members.

Manager Fiduciary Duties. As described above, the Operating Agreement contractually limits the Manager’s fiduciary duties and liability to the maximum extent permitted by Delaware law. By executing the subscription documents, each investor consents to such limitations.

The Operating Agreement sets forth the rights, duties, and limitations of the Manager with respect to conflicts of interest. By executing the Subscription Agreement, each investor acknowledges and consents to the existence of these conflicts and the resolution of these conflicts as set forth in the Operating Agreement.

articles.title: CERTAIN U.S. FEDERAL INCOME TAX CONSIDERATIONS

runs.text: The following is a brief summary of certain U.S. federal income tax considerations relevant to an investment in the SPV. This summary is general in nature, is not exhaustive, and does not constitute tax advice. Each prospective investor should consult its own tax advisor regarding the U.S. federal, state, local, and non-U.S. tax consequences of an investment in the SPV in light of its particular circumstances.
A. Classification of the SPV

The SPV will be classified as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes (and not as a publicly traded partnership taxable as a corporation). Each Member will be required to take into account its allocable share of the SPV’s items of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit, regardless of whether the SPV makes any distributions in any particular year (although Tax Distributions will be made under Section 5.6 to the extent Distributable Cash is available).
B. Class A Profits Interest

The Class A Unit issued to the Manager is intended to constitute a “profits interest” within the meaning of IRS Revenue Procedure 93-27 and Revenue Procedure 2001-43. If properly structured, the issuance of the Class A Unit should not result in taxable income to the Manager at the time of grant or to the SPV upon issuance. There can be no assurance that the IRS will respect this characterization.
C. Taxation of the Series Seed Preferred and Warrants

The Series Seed Preferred is expected to be treated as equity in a domestic C corporation. Distributions paid by Simphonic in respect of the Series Seed Preferred (including, potentially, RPR distributions) generally will be characterized in accordance with applicable Code provisions, which may treat such distributions as dividends, returns of capital, or capital gains depending on Simphonic’s earnings and profits and other factors. The Warrants generally will not give rise to current taxable income solely as a result of issuance, but the allocation of basis between the Series Seed Preferred and the Warrants and the timing and character of income on Warrant exercise will depend on the facts. Investors should consult their tax advisors regarding the treatment of the RPR and the Warrants.
D. Section 1202 (QSBS)

To the extent the Series Seed Preferred (and any Common Stock issued upon exercise of the Warrants) qualifies as “qualified small business stock” within the meaning of Section 1202 of the Code (“QSBS”), and assuming all other applicable requirements are met, certain U.S. individual investors may be eligible to exclude all or a portion of any gain on the sale of such stock from gross income for U.S. federal income tax purposes, subject to applicable holding period and dollar limitations. There can be no assurance that the Series Seed Preferred or any Warrant Shares will so qualify. Investors should consult their own tax advisors regarding the application of Section 1202.
E. Partnership Audit Rules; Section 6226 Election

Pursuant to Section 7.4 of the Operating Agreement, AltSpot Capital, LLC will serve as the Tax Representative under Section 6223(a) of the Code. The Members acknowledge in Section 7.4.3 that the SPV intends to elect the application of Section 6226 of the Code (push-out election). As a result, any IRS adjustment to the SPV’s items of income or deduction will be allocated to the Members for the reviewed year, and Members will be required to take such adjustments into account on their personal returns. Members are required to indemnify the SPV, the Manager, and the Tax Representative against tax liabilities (including penalties and interest) resulting from the Member’s failure to comply, including failure to report adjustments and failure to provide tax-related information requested by the Tax Representative. Members may be required to file amended returns and pay related taxes.
F. Tax Distributions

Section 5.6 of the Operating Agreement provides for mandatory Tax Distributions when Distributable Cash is available, sufficient to enable each Member to satisfy its estimated federal and state income tax liability with respect to allocations from the SPV (calculated assuming the highest applicable marginal rates). Tax Distributions are credited against later distributions under Section 5.7.
G. Schedule K-1; Withholding

The SPV will furnish each Member with an annual IRS Schedule K-1 (or successor form) reporting such Member’s allocable share of the SPV’s tax items. Pursuant to Section 7.2, this information will be sent within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year, although in practice K-1s may be issued later if Simphonic’s tax information is delayed. Members may need to file extensions for their personal returns. The SPV may be required to withhold taxes on certain allocations or distributions, including with respect to non-U.S. investors.
H. State and Local Taxes; Non-U.S. Investors

Investors may be subject to state, local, and non-U.S. tax filing and payment obligations as a result of an investment in the SPV. Non-U.S. investors should consult their own advisors regarding withholding obligations under FATCA, Section 1446(f), and other provisions.

articles.title: ERISA AND BENEFIT PLAN INVESTOR CONSIDERATIONS

runs.text: Investors that are “benefit plan investors” within the meaning of ERISA and Section 4975 of the Code, including (i) employee benefit plans subject to Title I of ERISA, (ii) plans subject to Section 4975 of the Code (including individual retirement accounts), and (iii) entities whose underlying assets include “plan assets” by reason of investment by such plans (“Benefit Plan Investors”), should carefully consider the particular fiduciary, prohibited transaction, unrelated business taxable income, and reporting issues associated with an investment in the SPV.

The Manager intends to monitor and limit investment in the SPV by Benefit Plan Investors so that participation by such investors does not equal or exceed 25% of the value of any class of equity interests in the SPV (or to otherwise rely on an applicable exception under the U.S. Department of Labor’s plan asset regulations). The Manager reserves the right to reject or limit subscriptions from Benefit Plan Investors, and to require redemption of Interests held by Benefit Plan Investors, in order to prevent the SPV’s assets from being treated as “plan assets.” Each prospective Benefit Plan Investor should consult its own counsel.

The Interests have not been registered under the Securities Act or any state securities laws and are being offered and sold in reliance on exemptions therefrom. Accordingly, the Interests are “restricted securities” within the meaning of Rule 144 under the Securities Act and may not be resold, pledged, hypothecated, or otherwise transferred unless registered under the Securities Act and applicable state securities laws or pursuant to an available exemption.

Article 6 of the Operating Agreement imposes additional restrictions on transfer. No Member may transfer, assign, convey, sell, encumber, or otherwise alienate its Interests, or any options, warrants, or other rights to acquire Interests, without the prior written consent of the Manager (not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed). Such consent is not required, however, for transfers to a Member’s spouse, parent, sibling, in-law, child, step-child, or grandchild, or to a trust for the benefit of the assigning Member or any of the foregoing family members (each, a “Family Member”). Any transferee that is not a Permitted Transferee admitted as a substitute Member in accordance with Section 6.2 will receive only an economic interest, without voting or consent rights.

In addition, no transfer or sale of any Interests is permitted unless the Member provides the Manager with an opinion of counsel that the proposed transfer (a) does not affect the original sale of the Interest under the Section 4(a)(2) exemption, and (b) is in compliance with all applicable state and federal securities laws (Section 10.5).

The underlying Series Seed Preferred and Warrants may be subject to additional transfer restrictions under the Definitive Documents. Investors must be prepared to bear the economic risk of an investment in the Interests for an indefinite period.

Pursuant to Section 7.2 of the Operating Agreement, the SPV will provide each Member, within 90 days after the end of each fiscal year, with: (i) information necessary to complete the Member’s federal and state income tax returns; and (ii) a copy of the SPV’s federal, state, and local income tax or information returns for the year. Section 7.1 also requires the SPV to maintain at its principal office customary books and records, including a list of Members and their capital contributions, the Certificate of Formation, the Operating Agreement, tax returns and financial statements for the seven (7) most recent fiscal years, and books and records for the current and past four (4) fiscal years.
The Manager intends, in addition (and in its discretion):

Annual Reports. To provide an annual report containing unaudited financial information of the SPV and a brief summary of material developments concerning Simphonic, in each case to the extent permitted by Simphonic and applicable confidentiality undertakings.
RPR Updates. To the extent the SPV receives RPR distributions from Simphonic, to provide periodic updates regarding such distributions and the cumulative RPR returns relative to the 1.5x cap.

Material Developments. To provide such other notices regarding material developments at Simphonic or the SPV as the Manager determines to be appropriate (including notice of a Qualifying Up Round, an exit transaction, a drag-along event, or a capital call).
The SPV does not currently expect to prepare audited financial statements unless required by applicable law or otherwise determined by the Manager.
The Interests are being offered directly by the SPV through the Manager and its affiliates without the use of an underwriter or placement agent.

The Offering is being made in reliance on the exemption from registration provided by Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act and Regulation D promulgated thereunder, and applicable state securities law exemptions, including without limitation Section 25102(f) of the California Corporate Securities Law of 1968. The SPV will rely on Rule 506(c) (which permits general solicitation but requires that all purchasers be verified accredited investors). Investors will be required to confirm their investor status in the Subscription Agreement and to provide such additional documentation as the Manager may require.
Persons interested in subscribing for Interests should follow the procedures set forth below:

Review the Offering Documents. Carefully review this Memorandum, the Operating Agreement, the Term Sheet, and the Subscription Agreement, together with such investor’s own legal, tax, and financial advisors.

Complete the Subscription Agreement. Complete, execute, and return the Subscription Agreement (which incorporates the Member representations, warranties, and covenants set forth in Article 10 of the Operating Agreement, including representations as to accredited investor status, preexisting relationship or experience, investment intent, restricted security, investment risk, disclosure, consultation with advisors, and tax consequences). The Manager may require additional investor questionnaires and documentation to satisfy anti-money laundering and other compliance requirements.

Fund the Subscription. Wire the subscription amount (minimum $50,000, subject to the Manager’s discretion to accept a lesser amount) to the SPV’s designated account in accordance with wire instructions provided by the Manager.

Acceptance. Subscriptions are not binding on the SPV until accepted by the Manager. The Manager may accept or reject any subscription, in whole or in part, in its sole discretion. If a subscription is rejected, or if the Series Seed Preferred financing fails to close, subscription funds will be returned without interest or deduction (less any actual SPV expenses, to the extent provided in the Operating Agreement).

The Manager intends to coordinate the SPV’s closing schedule with Simphonic’s Series Seed Preferred closing, which is targeted to occur no later than June 1, 2026 (subject to extension by Simphonic in its sole discretion). After the initial closing, additional Members may be admitted under Article 3 of the Operating Agreement on such terms as the Manager determines, subject to the Operating Agreement and applicable law.

The Interests are being offered only to investors who meet certain suitability standards, which mirror the representations and warranties required of each Member under Article 10 of the Operating Agreement. To qualify, each prospective investor must, at a minimum, represent and warrant that the investor:
Is an “Accredited Investor” as defined in Rule 501(a) of Regulation D under the Securities Act (Section 10.1).

Has either (i) a preexisting personal or business relationship with the SPV or one or more of its control persons, or (ii) by reason of the Member’s business or financial experience (or that of an unaffiliated, uncompensated financial advisor), is capable of evaluating the risks and merits of the investment and protecting the Member’s own interests (Section 10.2).
Is acquiring the Interest for investment purposes for the Member’s own account only and not with a view to or for sale in connection with any distribution thereof (Section 10.3).
Acknowledges that the Interest is a “restricted security” and may be held indefinitely (Sections 10.4, 10.5).
Has the financial ability to bear the economic risk of the investment, including a complete loss thereof, and acknowledges the speculative nature of the investment (Section 10.6).

Has had access to such information regarding the SPV and Simphonic as it has deemed necessary, has had the opportunity to ask questions, and has been advised to consult with such Member’s own legal and financial advisors (Sections 10.7, 10.8).
Acknowledges that the tax consequences of investing in the SPV depend on the Member’s particular circumstances and that the Member is relying solely on its own advisors (Section 10.9).
If a non-U.S. person, satisfies all applicable requirements under Regulation S and any applicable laws of its jurisdiction of residence.

The Manager may, in its sole discretion, impose additional or different suitability standards. Satisfaction of the standards set forth above does not necessarily mean that an investment in the SPV is suitable for any particular investor.

Each prospective investor is invited to ask questions of, and receive answers from, the Manager concerning the terms and conditions of the Offering, and to obtain such additional information about the SPV and Simphonic as the prospective investor may reasonably request, to the extent the Manager possesses such information or can acquire it without unreasonable effort or expense and is permitted to share it under applicable confidentiality and securities law constraints.
